awd_abstract_narration:
This award will support participation of early career scientists in Ribosomes 2025, this year's triennial international conference on ribosome research. The conference will be held at the Asilomar Conference Grounds in Pacific Grove, CA on June 22-27, 2025. Ribosomes are the molecular machines that translate genetic information carried in messenger RNA into protein in all living organisms, thus serving as the vital link between genotype and phenotype. The purpose of this conference is to bring together researchers from all over the world to communicate their latest findings to each other, and to stimulate critical discussion and promote collaboration. The gathering will provide a unique opportunity for graduate students and postdoctoral scholars to present new results of their research and to advance knowledge through engagement with peers and leaders in the ribosome field.

Ribosomes are the largest, most complex asymmetric biomolecular structures, presenting many daunting challenges to scientists investigating their form and function in living systems. The conference will enable researchers to share expertise across many disciplines, including foundational knowledge and new technological developments that advance ribosome biology and the fields of protein synthesis and gene expression at large.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Outcomes Report for the Ribosomes 2025 International Conference

Ribosomes are the molecular machines that translate the genetic information encoded in messenger RNAs into protein in every living organism on our planet, playing a key role in the most basic mechanism of life. Every three years since 1968, ribosome researchers have met at an international conference to share their latest discoveries.  This triennial conference is hosted by different scientists throughout the international ribosome community. This year, it was hosted by researchers from the University of California, Santa Cruz, and held at the Asilomar Conference Grounds in Pacific Grove, California from June 22-27, 2025. It was attended by over 200 scientists, including leading researchers from all over the world and their students and postdoctoral fellows. Each day, researchers presented their latest work in oral presentations and in poster sessions. In addition, there were numerous opportunities for stimulating informal discussions and exchange of scientific information. Support from the NSF made it possible for participation by many graduate students and other young researchers who might have otherwise not been able to attend. This enabled them to present their own findings, learn about the latest exciting discoveries directly from the scientists whose labs are responsible for them, and provided opportunities for them to meet many of the leaders in the ribosome field face to face. This support thus represents an important investment in the future of ribosome research.
